canonicalExplanation.summary: The browser reads HTML top to bottom. A plain `<script>` **pauses parsing**, runs, then parsing continues — so it can't see elements that come **after** it. `defer` downloads the script in parallel and runs it **after** the HTML is parsed, in document order. `console.log()` writes to the DevTools Console so you can observe what your code does and when.

sections.heading: Start here
sections.body:
You add `<script src="app.js">` in the head. It says `document.querySelector("#start")` is `null` — but the button is right there on the page! When the script ran, the parser hadn't reached the button yet. A deferred classic script runs after parsing while preserving document order. In this lesson you'll attach and run a script, then explain source order and observable output.

```predict
{"question": "`<script>` in the head (no defer) runs `console.log(document.querySelector(\"button\"))`. The button is in the body. Output?", "options": ["The button element", "null — the button hasn't been parsed yet"], "answer": 1, "why": "A classic script without defer runs the moment the parser reaches it, before later HTML exists."}
```

sections.heading: Before you begin
sections.body: You should know **Source-to-execution models** (how source becomes running code) and **Standards-mode document skeleton** (head vs body).

sections.heading: The model: parse, pause, run — or defer
sections.body:
```html
<head>
  <script src="a.js" defer></script>   <!-- runs 1st, after parsing -->
  <script src="b.js" defer></script>   <!-- runs 2nd -->
</head>
<body>
  <button id="start">Start</button>
</body>
```

```js
// a.js
const btn = document.querySelector("#start");
console.log("found:", btn);          // found: <button id="start">…
```

| Script type | When it runs | Order |
|---|---|---|
| classic (no attribute). | immediately, pausing the parser. | document order. |
| `defer`. | after HTML parsing finishes. | document order. |
| `async`. | as soon as it downloads. | not guaranteed. |
| `type="module"`. | deferred by default. | document order. |

```reveal
{"prompt": "Where do you see console.log output?", "answer": "In the browser's DevTools → Console tab (F12 or Ctrl+Shift+J / Cmd+Option+J)."}
```

sections.heading: Observe the order

includes: Attach scripts with and without defer and predict when they run.
Use console.log to observe execution order and output.

outcomes: Attach and run a script, then explain source order and observable output.

examples.title: A deferred script that finds its button
examples.situation: A deferred classic script runs after parsing while preserving document order.
walkthrough: **Problem:** `<script src="app.js">` in the head logs `null` for `#start` — the parser hasn't reached the button.
**Fix:** add `defer`; the script downloads in parallel and will run after parsing completes.
**Observe:** the Console now logs `found: <button id="start">`, and a second deferred script runs after it, preserving document order.
examples.result: The script finds the button, and multiple deferred scripts run in the order they appear.

examples.title: The analytics script that blocked the page
examples.situation: A large classic script in the head delays the whole page by two seconds on slow connections.
walkthrough: Classic scripts block the parser while they download and run.
Nothing below it renders until it finishes.
Fix: `defer` (or `async` if order doesn't matter), so parsing and rendering continue.
examples.result: The page appears immediately and the script runs afterwards.

misconceptions.mistakenBelief: Every script tag executes immediately, before the browser parses later HTML.
misconceptions.correction: Only classic scripts without defer or async run immediately and block parsing. defer runs after parsing in document order; async runs when downloaded; module scripts are deferred by default.
misconceptions.diagnosticPrompt: In "A deferred script that finds its button", why did the original script log null?

analogy.example: A classic script is like a **tour guide who stops the group mid-tour to give a speech** — nobody moves until it's done, and they can't talk about rooms not yet visited. defer is a guide who **waits until the whole tour is done**, then explains everything in order.
usefulFor: defer = run after parsing, in order
limitations: Tours don't download; scripts do, in parallel with defer.
async is a guide who talks whenever they arrive, out of order.

steps.explanation: The deferred classic script downloads without pausing parsing.
The parser reaches the button and adds it to the document.
The script runs after parsing while preserving document order.

trace.textAlternative: Running a deferred script. Step 1, Download: app.js is downloading in parallel; parser is continues. The deferred classic script downloads without pausing parsing. Step 2, Parse: #start is created in the DOM. The parser reaches the button and adds it to the document. Step 3, Run: console is found: <button id=start>. The script runs after parsing while preserving document order.

nearTransfer.prompt: Three scripts: `a.js` (classic, in head), `b.js` (defer), `c.js` (classic, end of body). Each logs its name. Predict the order.
expectedEvidence: a runs in the head; c at the end of body; b after parsing.

recap.summary: To attach and run a script and explain its output, remember classic scripts run immediately and block parsing, defer runs after parsing in document order, async runs when downloaded, and console.log shows what happened and when.
